test_policy.notes: Rose-Hulman "does not require standardized test scores for admission"; scores can be self-reported on the application or sent through the College Board or ACT, and submitted scores are reviewed together with course rigor, subject mastery and personal character. International applicants who need an English test can use SAT or ACT scores instead (see English).

requirements.notes: Apply with the GoRose App or the Common App (no preference for either; submit through only one). A completed application has the application, the high school transcript, one letter of recommendation from a teacher, counselor or principal (a homeschooled student needs someone other than a parent), and the $65 fee or a qualified fee waiver; the pages do not mention a required essay or a mid-year report. Course expectations: four years of math and English, three of lab science (biology, chemistry and physics), two of social science. International applicants also send a bank statement dated within six months (account holder name, amount, currency, English or certified translation) and, after admission, an affidavit of support; the funds must be readily available and cannot come from jobs or internships after arriving. Interviews through InitialView are optional ("applicants without one are at no disadvantage"). The pages print no admission year; the dates below are read as the current (fall 2027) cycle.

deadlines.label: Early Action (non-binding)
deadlines.notes: Notification on or before Dec 15 (international page). Applicants who miss a required item by the deadline are rolled to Regular Decision. The Provost Scholarship (biology, chemistry, biochemistry, biomath, math, physics) requires applying by this date. The page prints month and day only; read as Nov 1, 2026. Same dates for international applicants.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: The page prints month and day only; read as Feb 1, 2027. No Regular Decision notification date is published on the pages opened. Same date for international applicants.

deadlines.label: Enrollment deposit
deadlines.notes: Non-refundable, credited toward tuition and fees; the housing application follows after May 1.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required if English is not your native language. Exempt if you score 500 or higher on the SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing section or 21 or higher on the ACT English section; all other international applicants for whom English is a second language must submit TOEFL or IELTS scores (Duolingo and PTE Academic minimums are also listed).

english.notes: For tests taken before January 21, 2026: 88 internet-based with at least 20 in each section.
For tests taken on or after January 21, 2026: 4.5 with at least 4 in each section.

toefl.note: The admissions pages opened print SAT and ACT codes but no TOEFL institution code.

aid.notes: The international page says Rose-Hulman offers significant merit scholarships to every applicant but cannot meet full financial need; international students are on average responsible for about $45,000 a year, and full-tuition or full-ride awards are extremely limited. All admitted students are automatically considered for the Rose-Hulman Merit Scholarship (curriculum, class rank, test scores and activities). The Rose-Hulman Need-Based Grant is determined by the FAFSA, and the pages do not say whether international students qualify, while the Common Data Set (H6) ticks both institutional need-based and non-need-based aid for nonresident undergraduates (188 received aid, average $29,730; H7 asks nonresident aid applicants for the International Student's Certification of Finances). The page states no need-blind or need-aware policy for internationals, so none is recorded. The Provost Scholarship adds $10,000-$20,000 for applicants to biology, chemistry, biochemistry, biomath, math or physics who apply by Nov 1.

tier_notes.engineering: Our estimate: the school's own page states "No. 1 in Best Undergraduate Engineering Programs" (U.S. News, 2027 edition) and it offers civil, chemical, mechanical, electrical, computer, biomedical, optical and nano engineering; placed in the 16-40 band nationally.
tier_notes.computer_science: Our estimate: Computer Science, International Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence majors (majors list); no ranking cited, placed in the 41-100 band.
tier_notes.biology_life_sci: Our estimate: Biology, Biochemistry and Biomathematics majors at a small STEM school; no ranking cited, placed in the D band.
tier_notes.pre_med: Our estimate: no pre-med major or medical school link is listed; placed in the D band.
tier_notes.math_physics: Our estimate: Mathematics and Physics majors (majors list); no ranking cited, placed in the 41-100 band.
tier_notes.business: No business major; the undergraduate majors list has none.
tier_notes.economics: No economics major; the undergraduate majors list has none.
tier_notes.humanities: No humanities major; humanities appear only as minors (the undergraduate majors list has none).
tier_notes.arts_design: No arts or design major; the undergraduate majors list has none.
